properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/07/2025 to SWN PROD CO LLC in Cogan House Township, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SWN PROD CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/07/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8244481
Permit API: 081-22038
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/07/2025
Comments: On August 7, 2025, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection to a reported spill at the Expand Energy Elly May Well Pad. On August 6, 2025 at 1638, Expand Energy reported to the spill hotline that fluid with elevated conductivity was found outside of the containment on the well pad surface. Expand Energy estimated that approximately 32 gallons was leaked outside of the containment. Upon arrival at the well pad, Expand was vacuuming out the suspected containment causing the leak to the well pad. DEP screened the conductivity of the free liquid that had pooled next to the secondary containment and resulted in 2,570 uS/cm. The area where the free liquid had pooled next to the secondary containment was about 25 feet by 15 feet. After the containment was completely emptied and moved to determine the extent of the leak, a small hole was found in the plastic liner of the containment. Expand then vacuumed up the free liquid on the well pad surface. Mike Deming with Expand Energy arrived shortly after the free liquid had been vacuumed from the well pad surface. Mr. Deming explained that Expand had recently washed down the timber mats in this secondary containment. So the water leaking from containment was a mixture of wash down water and rainwater. Mr. Deming said that Expand expects to have a piece of machinery at the well pad by noon to begin excavating the contaminated soil in the area of impact. Mr. Deming said that Creston Environmental was scheduled to delineate the spill and confirm the remediation of the spill. DEP left the site prior to Expand beginning the excavation of the area of impact. At 1445, Mr. Deming called DEP to report the area of impact had been excavated. In an email provided by Mr. Deming, the area of excavation was approximately 19' by 29' with an average depth of 4". The conductivity of the soil after scraping the contaminated soil from the area of impact was less than 450 uS/cm. Mr. Deming said approximately 8.75 tons of contaminated soil was placed in a lined dumpster. Based on the amount of contaminated soil removed and the calculation completed for the amount of liquid that soil could hold, 32 gallons is the volume leaked from containment onto the well pad surface. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 have been noted. Due to the immediate remediation of the spill the violations are considered corrected.

Comments: On January 7, 2019, Department representatives Brad Kline and Jared Jacobini conducted an investigation of the reported spill on PGE Company LLC. Moore Rd. Ext. The Department met Chris Earley and Chad Oechler with PGE. A tanker truck was hauling production fluids from COP Tract 729 Pad E, as the truck was driving down the access road a valve failed on the tank. This caused about 2-3 barrels of production fluid to spill on Moore Rd. Ext. The tanker truck also spilled about 10 gallons on COP Tract 729 Pad E. At the time of the investigation, the soil could be seen stained about 40 yds x 15 yds. Specific conductivity measurements were taken in the area of the affected soil with a range of 2.1 mS/cm to 4.0 mS/cm. 4.0 mS/cm is the upper limit of the Department's meter. Specific conductivity was also measured in UNT to Ramsey with a reading of 25.2 uS/cm. UNT to Ramsey run pH measured 7.6. At the time of the measurements, UNT to Ramsey Run appeared unaffected by the spill. PGE had a contractor there removing the contaminated soil with Moody and Associates delineating the spill area on Moore Rd. Ext. The contaminated soil was excavated off Pad E and placed on plastic to be loaded in a roll back dumpster. The release of production fluid is considered a violation since the estimated volume is over 42 gallons. PGE is required to go through the Act 2 process.

Comments: On March 10 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the CFR/USX 5 OG Well in regards to OGI referral.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department traveled down the access road towards the well site. Approximately halfway down the access road, the Department observed water flowing onto the access road. The water was observed continuing to flow down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water.Upon further inspection, the water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet. Based on these observations, it appears the water is flowing from the drainage channel/trib to Antram Run onto the access road rather than through the culvert.Upon further inspection of the well site, the well appeared equipped for production. Violation ID: 900918
Permit API: 083-57192
Unconventional: No

Municipality: Sergeant Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/02/2020
Comments: The operator called the Department to report a spill at the Burning Well PV-81 well site on December 2nd at 9:20 am. The Complaint ID for this spill is #353829.A tree near the well fell due to heavy snow and wind overnight onto the lead line of the well, causing a union to fail. The well is pumped with an electric powered pumpjack that is on a timer. This well begins to pump at 8:00 am. At 8:30 am, the well pumper came by and found the well leaking. He immediately shut the well in and informed the operator of the spill. The tree was cut off the line and the flow of oil was stopped. Dave Hill plus two well pumpers from PVE were on site when I arrived, as were three representatives of Howard Drilling, who had been called to help clean the oil up. They were using a portable vacuum tank to collect any loose oil they could find. The oil appears to be caught in the snow in an area approximately 15-20 feet circular down gradient from the spot of the leak. No oil flowed outside this area, as heavy snow acted to slow and prevent seepage. It appears as though 10-20 gallons of crude oil was spilled from the compromised line. The operator has cleared the top of the tree from this area to begin cleanup. Snow and debris have been cleared at the edge of the contaminated area. The operator has placed a continuous pile of absorbent peat in this cleared area around the spill as a berm. They intend to rake and shovel the oily snow and debris to the center of the area, then load it into two or more plastic totes that will be used as temporary storage. The entire area will then be covered again with peat for the time being. When conditions allow, they intend to dig up any soil that is contaminated and haul it to the landfill, along with the oil covered sticks from the site. Continued inspection will be performed on this site as cleanup progresses. See attached sheet for violations.

Comments: On January 5 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Ziolkowoski Well Site (NOT approved on 11/6/2023) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/4/2026 (CTS 394386). Present during the inspection was operator representative Nate Smiell.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel. The Department was unable to assess site stabilization due to snow coverage.At the time of inspection, there are 14 total wells on the well pad. According to Mr. Smiell, 8 of the wells (2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H, and 9H) are completed/active wells. These wells were surrounded by protective barriers and appeared equipped for productions with well tags present. Mr. Smeill stated that stimulation for the other 6 wells (1H,10H,11H,12H,13H, and 14H) has been completed and they are currently in the process of drill outs for these wells.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Smiell guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Smiell the release occurred on 1/4/2026. He stated the release was caused by 2 loose flange bolts on a 2-inch oil dump line located at the front of the #5 GPU. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water and condensate mixture released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot radius around the #5 GPU. A background conductivity reading of 0.08mS was obtained. Conductivity readings of 2.76mS, 10.36mS, 2.14mS, and several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed active remediation of the spill occurring. Mr. Smiell stated that an air excavation/vacuum truck was being used to break up the ground and vacuum the contaminated material into waste containers. He stated that additional excavation by heavy machinery will occur as needed when the GPU is removed from its location as they plan to replace it upon competition of the active drill outs.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

These wells were surrounded by protective barriers and appeared equipped for productions with well tags present. Mr. Smeill stated that stimulation for the other 6 wells (1H,10H,11H,12H,13H, and 14H) has been completed and they are currently in the process of drill outs for these wells.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Smiell guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Smiell the release occurred on 1/4/2026. He stated the release was caused by 2 loose flange bolts on a 2-inch oil dump line located at the front of the #5 GPU. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water and condensate mixture released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot radius around the #5 GPU. A background conductivity reading of 0.08mS was obtained. Conductivity readings of 2.76mS, 10.36mS, 2.14mS, and several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed active remediation of the spill occurring. Mr. Smiell stated that an air excavation/vacuum truck was being used to break up the ground and vacuum the contaminated material into waste containers. He stated that additional excavation by heavy machinery will occur as needed when the GPU is removed from its location as they plan to replace it upon competition of the active drill outs.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

SPSI was dispatched to remediate the off containment spill and a vacuum truck was already on site to remove what was lost to secondary containment.According to the operator 1,043 gallons was removed from secondary containment. 5-7 gallons is reported to have been lost off containment.On my arrival I was met by operator representative Brandon Carson and Jason Dockum Water Supervisor. Inspection Date: 08/31/2020
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 8/30/2020 at approximately 3:30 PM. According to the operator, due to human error a shut valve was left open which allowed reuse water to travel from the tank pad to the well pad storage tanks which then over flowed into secondary containment. An additional amount appeared to splash off into the R3 riprap adjacent to the secondary containment. SPSI was dispatched to remediate the off containment spill and a vacuum truck was already on site to remove what was lost to secondary containment.According to the operator 1,043 gallons was removed from secondary containment. 5-7 gallons is reported to have been lost off containment.On my arrival I was met by operator representative Brandon Carson and Jason Dockum Water Supervisor. The site is actively being frac'd, but is down for an inspection. SPSI is not on site, the operator reports that remediation efforts have been completed and a single roll off box is awaiting pick up (Photo 10).The ERP is on site in the mailbox. Safety Data Sheets are located in the trailer along with the secondary containment log (Photo 9). The secondary containment was inspected on both 8/30 and 8/31. No leaks to containment were reported and no visible leaks are currently observed.There is still a rust colored fluid in secondary containment (Photo 2). According to the operator, the mats are being washed off and a vac truck is on site to remove the water. The operator reports that this is not from the spill incident.The operator reports that the over flow was observed immediately and the shut in valve to the storm drain was closed (Photo 4). Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There are two post-construction stormwater management structures onsite. They appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine gas processing units (GPUs) held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: Inspection Report 1 of 2On 03/03/2026, a routine partial inspection was conducted at the John Hunter Well Site in Donegal Township, Washington County (37-125-28285). I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Sara Trio (PA DEP).The following was observed:-Act 9 sign (Photo 1).-Sediment-laden water flowing from access road and site to culvert inlet (Photos 2-4). Recommend access road maintenance.-Culvert inlet pipe receiving road fines and sediment-laden water (Photos 5,6).-Culvert outlet area appears to be pooling/discharging sediment; visible from access road (Photos 7,8). Recommend maintenance and adequately functioning environmental controls design and application in all drainage areas.-Accelerated erosion flow path downslope from culvert outlet (Photos 9-11).-Existing Compost Filter Sock (CFS) appears overtaken by wood debris and vegetation; sediment deposition from what appears to be significant flow downslope (Photos 12,13). Recommend maintenance and adequately functioning environmental controls design and application in all drainage areas.-Flow path of sediment-laden water continued downslope (Photos 14-16).-Sediment deposit concentrated area (Photos 17,18).-Flow path of sediment-laden water discharging into unnamed tributary flowing to Little Wheeling Creek (Photos 19,20).-Further down access road toward pad, culvert inlet and outlet related to inspection report 2 of 2 appears receiving and discharging sediment-laden water; accelerated erosion and sediment flow path downslope into wooded area offsite (Photos 21,22).Range Resources Environmental Compliance Specialist Dennis Furmanek was contacted on 03/04/2026 regarding observations noted above.Recommendations as noted above.Due to the discharge of sediment from the site capable of reaching waters of the Commonwealth and failure to minimize accelerated erosion and sedimentation, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), 78a.53, 102.4(b)4, 102.11(A)2, CSL 301, and CSL 307(a) are being issued.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Comments: On April 30, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation of Diversified's Benninger 11 plugged well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following IR 4058495 where violations were issued for failure to comply with an order of the Department for failing to submit a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) within 60 days of restoration.According to Department records, this well was plugged on 5/14/2024, therefore the well site should have been fully restored by 2/14/2025 and a WSRR submitted no later than 4/15/2025.On 7/25/2024, the Department received a WSRR submission, however it was denied in IR 3876088 for an unrestored access road, during IR 3876088, the Department requested clarification from the Operator on whether the access road is proposed to remain. A WSRR was resubmitted on 5/29/2025 and on 9/23/2025, (documented in IR 4058495), the Department returned that WSRR due to Section E being filled out incorrectly. The Department also recommended during IR 4058495, that the Operator include with the WSRR the Department's Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration form 8000-FM-OOGM0020 which can be found on the DEP's eLibrary along with the previously submitted Affidavit in lieu of a landowner signature on the form.To date, a WSRR resubmission with the Department's landowner waiver form requesting the access road remain has yet to be received. A COA was entered into between the Department and Diversified on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, Diversified also shall submit Form 8000-PM-OOGM0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," to the Department within 60 days after the Well Site restoration in accordance with 25 Pa. Code 78.65(3) and 78a.65(e).At the time of this inspection, the Department utilized the plugged well's approximate GPS coordinates to locate the plugged well and observed the site restoration plan in the on-site mailbox and a graveled access road. The plugged well site was observed to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative cover with no erosion and sedimentation issues present. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from the plugged well's approximate location. No erosion and sediment control features nor production equipment was observed to remain on site.Based on today's inspection, it appears that the access road is still not restored and to date, the Department has yet to receive a WSRR resubmission with a Post-Plugging Landowner Wavier requesting the gravel road remain, therefore, violations issued for failure to comply with a COA with the Department for failing to submit a WSRR (with the LO waiver for the access road to remain unrestored) within 60 days of restoration is to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. Comments: On May 12, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4179368.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 2/23/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 11/23/2026 in accordance with current regulations.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S plans on site have not been updated as stated in the NOV Response (IR 4166188). The plans appear to be unchanged and do not include wetland delineations in any of the drawings or added wetland seed mix(es) to Detail 06.- CFS near the access road entrance is not properly installed at this time (Photo 5).- Gravel from the RCE remains on site. The Department recommends the operator remove all gravel that is not pre-existing from the site.- A berm appears to have been constructed (Photo 7). The Department requests information regarding the purpose of the berm and if it is to remain post-restoration.- The site appears to have been seeded and mulched, with vegetation growing in some areas at this time.- What appears to be third party disturbance in the form of a two track trail is observed from the access road through site, and exiting over CFS (Photos 7-8, 11, 13, 15, 23).- CFS surrounding the site is improperly installed (Photos 11, 12, 21) including portions that have been repaired multiple times causing the sock to flatten. The Department recommends the operator replace the repaired portions of CFS.- CFS where the surface water exits the site appears to be failing, showing signs of overtopping and undercutting. The Department recommends the operator replace the current CFS and properly maintain CFS on site until restoration is achieved.- The absorbent pads that were left on site by the operator appear to remain on site at this time. The Department recommends the operator remove the absorbent pads from the site.Violations remain outstanding at this time.

Violation ID: 863495

Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-17
Comments: The Department was on-site in response to the report of a spill incident of more than (5) gallons of diesel based drilling mud that occurred on 9/16/19 at 17:05 hours. The weather conditions are sunny skies with a light breeze, and temperatures in the upper 60's. Remediation of the impacted area affiliated with the spill was in progress. Resource Environmental of Montrose, PA is the Cabot subcontractor delineating the extent of the impact via the use of a photoionization detector (PID) meter to determine the presence of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds. H&P Flex Rig 259 is the drilling rig on the location. The current drilling depth of the M Powers 12H well is (4,351.59) feet. Cassidy Moyer, DEP WQS and I initially met with Mike Stansfield, Drilling Engineer of Cabot in the site office/company man trailer. Mr. Stansfield provided the following information relevant to site activities and the spill incident. "The rig is on the M Powers 12H well. Remediation of this well is in progress. The 4H and 8H wells will be drilled to total depth (TD). All other wells on the pad have been drilled to TD. A low cement top was found when a cement bond log was run. Perforations were shot in the production casing at (4,430) and (6,000) feet. Cement was pumped into the production casing and through the cement retainer. The cement retainer didn't hold in the production casing. The cement retainer was drilled out. Diesel based drilling mud overflowed the 12H well casing vent tank onto containment. Some of the mud got outside the containment. The mud came out of the top of the tank in the form of a flow, then rolled off the containment to the pad surface, and then it flowed under the containment. The spill volume is over (5) gallons, but may be under (42). We may be able to calculate the volume of the spill, and determine it is under (42) gallons. The spill happened around 5 PM yesterday. Marlon Droddy, the site company man found the spill and reported it to Mike Cromley, the site safety man. Remediation of the impacted area started last night. Initially, we were not able to dig under the vent lines. We eventually moved the vent tanks and the containment to evaluate the extent of the impact.” Resource Environmental provided the following information relevant to remediation of the impacted area. “We arrived here today at 9AM. A small excavation of the impacted area was done yesterday. The excavation is now at (5) feet below the ground surface of the pad. Three test pits have been dug to determine the extent of the impact. The test pits were excavated and backfilled North, South, and just next to the impacted area. The test pits were excavated to a depth of (5) feet. Visually impacted material was not observed in the test pits. The PID meter didn't detect any readings in the test pits. Initial PID reading of soil in the impacted area was (592) parts per million (PPM). The PID reading in the vent tank was (741) PPM. We use (25) PPM as a standard threshold. In addition to using a PID meter to guide the remediation, we will use visual and olfactory senses.” Steve Catalfamo of Cabot indicated impacted material will most likely be transported for disposal to Alliance Landfill in Taylor, PA, and Cabot will attempt to determine the volume of the spill. The Department left the site at 14:20.

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-23
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 887195
Permit API: 083-57162
Unconventional: Yes
County: McKean
Municipality: Sergeant Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-23
Comments: At 17:48 on Saturday (6/20/20), Doug Kepler reported a hose rupture on well pad D08-O that resulted in the discharge of 110-120 barrels of production fluid to containment. Doug Kepler reported about 8-10 barrels of fluid overflowed containment onto a gravel road. It was determined that the spill flowed for 3-4 minutes prior to being noted and then shut off. At the time of this inspection, the operator was in the process of removing the contaminated soil from the impacted area. The containment was vacuumed dry and then removed. A mini excavator and rolloff containers were brought on site. Screening was done of the impacted soil using a soil conductivity meter with a probe. It was determined that the production water flowed along the access road approximately 200-250 feet in a narrow band before exiting the road surface in a small depression. The operator had removed all the impacted soil in this stretch at the time of this inspection. They were loading their 11th container at this time. An excavation was developing deeper on the northeast side of the spill site, where elevated conductivity was noted several feet into the soil. The operator will continue to screen and remove soil today and for as long as necessary. Rolloff containers are being staged on the D08-O pad, which is just off the edge of the spill location. Further follow up of this spill location will be performed as necessary.
